name: Itutang
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Retired languoid (merged into Inapang mzu 2008); Glottolog bib holds only the ISO change request, no descriptive work.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Western Madang District, New Guinea. PhD thesis, ANU. (hdl 1885/130077, open)
sources.note: p.13 (p.22): same sentence as the 1971 book — stress marking omitted because 'the stress patterning has not been well established yet'; no Itutang-specific stress statement.
No grammar, sketch or phonology references; only Z'graggen 1969 (classification) and Campbell et al. 2022 (endangerment). Alternative names Inapang, Itutang, Midsivindi.
14 items, no stress marks; the forms (okarɨka, aßa, gai, ɲɨ, aɲi) do not match Z'graggen's Itutang wordlist and look like a mislabelled Iñapari (Arawakan) list; not usable.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-253: merge [itu] Itutang into [mzu] Inapang (submitted by Daniel Moore, New Tribes Mission). SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; identity only: 'Itutang is the name of one village within the Inapang language'; submitter cites three years of first-hand work with the group and no published sources.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: ANU. (hdl 1885/146484)
sources.note: Checklist of languages, villages and populations only (Itutang M5, Midsivindi M6); no phonology, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. (hdl 1885/146580, open ANU repository)
sources.note: p.6 (p.14), global disclaimer for the whole survey: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Itutang is language 59 (Tamolan family, pp.80-82); §2.23.22.3 'Typological characteristics of Tamolan' (p.82) gives only segmental notes plus 'Romkun is possibly tonal'; nothing on Itutang stress or tone.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Inapang language' (stub, cites Ethnologue 25th ed. only)
sources.note: Nothing; lists dialects Midsivindi, Itutang, Yigavesakama; 4,000 speakers (2016).

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 197-432. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher
sources.note: Most recent survey of Ramu languages incl. Tamolan; may carry a general note on Ramu word stress/tone that could be cited second-hand for Inapang.
sources.venue: The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide
